outcome: Mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: 530 pregnant women in urban regions of Urmia, Iran
finding: Socioeconomic factors, particularly family socioeconomic status, were the strongest predictors of choosing cesarean section delivery among Iranian urban women.
mod_finding: Women with higher socioeconomic status, whose husbands were employed in governmental organizations, who preferred private hospitals, and who expressed a preference for cesarean section during pregnancy were more likely to have a cesarean delivery.
